forceAngle_desc: Angle of pulling vector relative to horizontal axis (reduces normal contact force)

surfaceFriction_desc: Kinetic friction coefficient between crate and floor

workEnergyExpl: Net work of all combined forces equals change in kinetic energy
workIntegralExpl: Area under the force vs displacement curve
instantPowerExpl: Dot product of force vector and velocity vector
efficiencyExpl: Ratio of useful mechanical work to total input energy consumed
theoryContent:
Core Principles of Work, Power, and Efficiency:
1. Work (W): Work performed by a force is the component of force along displacement multiplied by distance (W = F·d·cosθ).
2. Work-Energy Theorem: The net work done by all acting forces equals the change in the object's kinetic energy (W_net = ΔK).
3. Power (P): The rate of doing work or transferring energy (P = dW/dt = F·v·cosθ). As velocity increases, maintaining the same force requires proportionally greater power.
4. Efficiency (η): Real motors dissipate input electrical energy into heat, yielding efficiency η = P_useful / P_input < 100%.
